title: Playing with Buddy Petit around the lake; George Lewis in Mandeville
summary: Asked about early dance bands, Robertson says he played with Buddy Petit, who had a boat run on the lake, and recalls George Lewis playing with them in Mandeville.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What about these dance orchestras? Did you play with any of the earlier dance orchestras, Mr. Robinson?
Like the dance bands? Who did you play with when years come by? Years ago.
Oh, I used to play with old Buddy P.T.
Oh, you did play with Buddy? Oh yeah, I played all over the lake then. When they had that boat run up in the man. Who did he have in his band then, at that time?

Oh yeah, he had that boat. One of the best clients that we had here, he left here and went to California. His wife died over the river not so long ago. Not good to know, he come from Manneville too, but I didn't know that boy.
Yeah, yeah. Used to play down in the, in the, in the, the, the, not so long. He stayed there quite a while. He was good, he had a band and he left the other one long. George Lewis?
Oh, George Lewis. George Lewis was playing with us. In Manneville. He used to play with us in Manneville. He said he's still alive. Yeah, he's still alive. Yeah, I know, but he left his wife's.
Yeah, he bought a home over the road and his wife died.

And he came back here and I haven't seen the hood of George Lewis. He still has his home there. He's out on the road now, right now. I ain't seen that man, right there in Manneville. That's why he came. I ain't seen him no more. I ain't seen that man since he needed to be with his wife. Really? I was at the funeral. I ain't seen him in that day to listen. George Lewis, I had a fella at that time we used to call him E-String. We used to call him E. We used to call him Big E. But he was playing with us.
